valueSets.context: The complete 6-row Selection | Description settings table on the Life to Date tab. INDENTED-TABLE CASE: the whole table sits inside numbered step 4, so a '^|' census returns 0 for this file and 22 with leading whitespace allowed. LABEL DRIFT on the fifth value: configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md writes the past-tense 'Matched against Received Quantity' in its overview bullet ('the admin can select the Line Item ' + EN-DASH + ' Receipt rule in the Rules tab and the Matched against Received Quantity rule in the Life to Date tab') and the present-tense 'Match against Received Quantity' in its own numbered step 33 lines later; the canonical settings table quoted here uses the present tense. valueSets.context: READING A of the Rules-tab Tolerance control - the FOUR-option bullet run under the heading 'Choose one tolerance:'. Complete and in source order. valueSets.sourceQuote: Within (+/-): Choose this to specify a balanced amount of tolerance equal above and below that of the PO field being matched to the same request field
valueSets.notes: CONTRADICTS READING B (next set): four options here versus three there, 'Within (+/-)' here versus 'Within' there, and Currency present here and absent there. NOT RECONCILED. The quote deliberately carries the two discriminating features - the '(+/-)' suffix and the option's existence as an independent bullet in a four-item list. Full source text of the other three: 'None: Choose this to trigger the rule if any deviation is detected between the fields - no tolerance is permitted'; 'Custom: Choose this to create an asymmetrical amount of tolerance above and below that of the PO field being matched to the same request field'; 'Currency: Choose the base currency your company uses. Conversions for alternate currencies used on incoming invoices will be calculated automatically and applied by the system.' Currency is arguably a different axis from None/Within/Custom - the source nevertheless lists all four under one 'Choose one tolerance:' heading, and that is recorded as found, not corrected. The whole section is marked conditional at the step level: '(Optional depending on field choice) Determine what tolerance you will allow when the rule is triggered using options under Tolerance.' - so a driver must not assume Tolerance is present for every Payment Request / Purchase Order field pair. CONSEQUENCE FOR A DRIVER: probe the four-option list first; if only three appear, match on the prefix 'Within' rather than the exact string 'Within (+/-)', and do not fail the step because Currency is missing.

valueSets.context: CATALOG A - the four confirmation types with their full definitions, published as a numbered prose list (not a table). Complete, in source order. Filed as a set rather than left flat because the definitions are what decide which type a rule should produce.
valueSets.sourceQuote: These outcomes are called confirmation types, and there are four types:
valueSets.notes: Verbatim definitions: None = 'No receipt confirmation is required. This is appropriate for spend requiring only a two-way match between invoice and PO.'; Invoice = 'Presenting and confirming the invoice overall, within Concur Invoice, is sufficient to confirm receipt. This is especially appropriate for some types of Service spend.' (the source continues with a routine-cleaning-services illustration); Receipt Central = 'The receipt (quantity) will be entered centrally and stored in the ERP, then passed to Concur Invoice. This is appropriate for goods received at a central warehouse, where the PO/Invoice Owner has no part in answering the question of Receipt.'; Receipt Individual = 'The receipt (quantity) will be entered by the PO/Invoice Owner in the ERP, then passed to Concur Invoice. This is appropriate for goods received directly by an individual at a home or regional office, or partial receipt of hours-based services.' HARD CONSTRAINT published with this catalog and easy to miss: 'Quantity received must be entered or stored in the ERP, and then passed to Concur Invoice through the Receipt Import. There is no interface available to directly enter quantities in Concur Invoice.' - Receipt Central and Receipt Individual are inert without an ERP feed. The type is chosen through the Edit Confirmation button: 'Do this by clicking Edit Confirmation to open the Select Confirmation Type window, choosing a confirmation type based on the rule group.'

valueSets.context: The complete 6-row Status Name | Description table - the closed catalog of outcomes a configured rule set can produce. valueSets.sourceQuote: The table below shows all possible Match Status types.
valueSets.notes: ALL SIX ROWS, NOTHING SAMPLED, source order. Verbatim descriptions: Matched = 'The invoice is associated to a PO and has no exceptions (note that several invoices can match a single PO).'; Does Not Match = 'The invoice is associated to a PO and has one or more exceptions (note that several invoices can match a single PO).'; Waiting for PO = 'The invoice is using a PO policy but the PO number on the invoice does not match any corresponding number on a PO.'; Pending Match = 'The invoice is using a PO policy and is associated to a PO, but not assigned to a user.'; Missing PO Number = 'The invoice is using a PO policy but is missing the PO number that associates it to a PO.'; No Match Required = 'The invoice uses a non-PO policy or has been deleted.' Three rows carry a SECOND explanatory paragraph in the same cell, not reproduced in the values: Waiting for PO adds 'This can happen when the PO Number value in a PO-based invoice is changed, causing the invoice association to a PO to be broken, and a new association not yet made.'; Pending Match adds 'This can happen if the invoice is newly created and not yet assigned, or if an existing invoice is assigned to a user without adequate policy rights'; Missing PO Number adds 'This can happen when the Payment Request import record has a value for External ID specified, but the purchase order number (PO #) field is blank in the feed.' Determination rule published with the table: Match Status 'is determined by' successful association to a PO - AND - presence of any match exceptions. Display surfaces named: 'Match Status displays on the My Invoices, Approve Invoice, Assign Invoice, and Processor List pages.' TOOLS-GUIDES ONLY - this catalog does not exist in admin-guides.

orphanCandidates.enumerates: Concur Receiving roles matrix - the complete 6-row x 4-column Role | What the User Can/Cannot Do | Where? | Conditions table published in this page's own tools-guides Required Roles topic.
values: Purchase Order Processor || Can add, edit, and delete receipts and receipt images. || In the transmitted purchase order. || None.
Invoice Processor || Can add, edit, and delete receipts and receipt images. || In Purchase Order tab of the opened invoice. || None.

Purchase Request User || Can add, edit, and delete receipts and receipt images || In the transmitted purchase order. || The admin must have selected (enabled) the Allow Purchase Request Owners to Edit their own Purchase Orders option in Invoice Settings. Alternatively, the user can have the Receipt User role.
Invoice User || Can add, edit, and delete receipts and receipt images. || In the Purchase Order tab of the opened invoice. || None.

Central Receiver || Can add, edit, and delete receipts and receipt images for all purchase orders in their group. Cannot transmit and process purchase orders or invoices. || In the transmitted purchase order. || The Concur Receiving feature must be activated.

Receipt User || Can add, edit, and delete receipts and receipt images. Can only add, edit, and delete receipt data for their own purchase orders. || In the transmitted purchase order. || The Concur Receiving feature must be activated.
orphanCandidates.whyNoOwner: None of these six roles is a control on either Group 3 page - role assignment happens in user administration, which is not a page in this graph. Attaching the matrix to rule_set_name (as one extraction lens did, defensively) would be a wrong owner: rule_set_name is a list-page column, not a role picker. ALL SIX ROWS AND ALL FOUR COLUMNS are reproduced above so the catalog is not silently lost; the ' || ' separator is MINE, added to keep one row per array entry, and every string between separators is verbatim except that the Purchase Request User's second cell genuinely lacks a trailing period in the source. Two multi-sentence cells (Central Receiver, Receipt User) are joined from two source paragraphs within one cell. Anchoring quote in the file: 'This table shows roles in Concur Invoice working with Concur Receiving and what they can and cannot do.' Also published in the same topic and worth carrying forward: 'Only the Invoice Configuration administrator can access and configure the Purchase Order Matching Rules feature.' and a Note that a user with the Purchase Order Processor or Purchase Order Processor (Audit) role can reach imported POs on entities without Purchase Request enabled. TOOLS-GUIDES ONLY - an admin-guides-skewed search loses this table entirely.
orphanCandidates.whatWouldFixIt: A Concur Receiving / Purchase Order page node (or a roles/permissions node) with a field that owns the role roster. The Purchase Request User row also carries a real cross-page dependency to the already-built Invoice Settings page, via the 'Allow Purchase Request Owners to Edit their own Purchase Orders' option - if a field of that name exists on Invoice Settings, this row can be wired as a dependency without inventing an owner here.

orphanCandidates.enumerates: The three matching METHODS the page's rule sets implement - a closed three-item catalog with definitions.
values: Two-Way Matching: Matching between invoices and purchase orders (no receipt)
Three-Way Matching: Matching between invoices and purchase orders and received quantities
Receipt Confirmation: Matching between invoices and purchase orders (including receipt confirmation that the order has been fully received)
orphanCandidates.whyNoOwner: NO CONTROL ANYWHERE IN THE CORPUS is labelled with these three names. They are the conceptual frame - achieved by which rules you switch on - not a dropdown, and the closest real field, matching_rule_type, has a different two-value list (Life to Date, Rules). Kept because it is a complete enumerated catalog and because it disambiguates the page's vocabulary for a driver. Anchoring quote: 'Concur Invoice offers three types of matching methods:'. Each of the three values above is verbatim, in source order. The tools-guides twin overview-8b4fd062.md republishes the same list nearly verbatim (differing only by 'Invoice does not check quantity' for 'Concur Invoice does not check quantity', a capitalised 'Suppliers', a missing abstract line and italics) - a cross-deliverable republish, NOT a UI variant, so it is not double-counted.
orphanCandidates.whatWouldFixIt: Nothing - and that is the finding. It should stay unwired unless SAP later documents a control that selects a matching method by name.

orphanCandidates.enumerates: The 6-term terminology glossary for this page's objects, published as a bullet run.
values: Concur Receiving: The ability for users to add quantity receipt data manually in Concur Invoice.
Purchase Order Payment Request: An invoice associated with a PO by the unique number associated with the PO.
Life to Date: The complete span of all invoices associated with their purchase order.
Associate: The relationship created when an invoice is linked to a PO by entering the unique PO number in the request header form.
Matching Rule Set: The combination of rules that is executed for every PO request matched under a given policy.
Named Rules Group: Any rule existing within ("under") the Matching Rule Set, for example, a condition-based rule group.
orphanCandidates.whyNoOwner: A glossary is not a field's option list. These are the authoritative object names for the page's node graph, not values an admin selects. Anchoring quote: 'The following terms are used throughout this document and within Invoice.' All six terms, verbatim and complete, in source order; the Matching Rule Set entry is cut at its first sentence, the source continuing 'Can be a simple, single rule, or more complex multiple match rule that includes "nested" condition-based rules run against custom fields that differentiate by spend type, project, or division as examples.' TERMINOLOGY TENSION worth flagging for a driver: 'Life to Date' is simultaneously a glossary concept, a tab name (life_to_date_tab) and a rule-type value (matching_rule_type), so a text match on those three words is ambiguous.
orphanCandidates.whatWouldFixIt: A glossary or vocabulary node type in the schema. It should never be wired to a field.

orphanCandidates.enumerates: The four events that RE-RUN an already-configured match rule set, and - separately - the three invoice states in which match rules CANNOT run at all.
values: On Header save and Line Item delete, save, and line sequence change
Changing Invoice Owner, Vendor, or reassigning an invoice
Upon PO import, if the import identifies a matching invoice in Concur Invoice that had not been previously associated to a PO
Upon receipt import for invoices associated to the PO
Is part of a payment demand
orphanCandidates.whyNoOwner: Runtime timing and eligibility, not a field's option list - no control on either Group 3 page selects when rules run. Kept in full because a driver needs it to predict when its configuration takes effect and why a correctly configured rule set can appear to do nothing. The two lists are concatenated in one record and are distinguishable by position: entries 1-4 are the re-run triggers, entries 5-7 the blocking states. Anchoring quotes: 'When these two things are true, rules are re-run whenever relevant changes are made to the invoice or to the PO. This includes:' and 'Has been extracted'. The seventh value keeps the source's markdown emphasis characters ('_Unassigned_') so it stays a verbatim substring. FIRST-RUN preconditions are separate and BOTH required: successful association to a PO - AND - the invoice in an assigned state; three-way matching adds association to received quantities. Published caveat: 'Rules are rerun for the changes listed above regardless of workflow status.' TOOLS-GUIDES ONLY.
orphanCandidates.whatWouldFixIt: A behaviour/trigger node type. As field values it has no owner and must not be given one.

orphanCandidates.enumerates: The four documented sources of documents that end up attached to a transmitted purchase order.
values: Administrators who configure purchase orders in PO Configuration
Users who create purchase requests and select the Include in PO Transmission option
Approvers who approve purchase requests and select the Include in PO Transmission option
PO processors who process purchase requests and select the Include in PO Transmission option
orphanCandidates.whyNoOwner: This is provenance, not an option list: the Supporting Document control on Purchase Order Configuration (roster field supporting_documents) is an upload/view/remove control with no enumerated values, and only the FIRST of these four entries is that control at all. Wiring all four to supporting_documents would assert that an admin picks a document source from a list, which the corpus never says. All four are verbatim and complete, in source order. This is the topic that independently attests the page by name and gives its nav path: 'the Invoice Configuration administrator uses the Purchase Order Configuration tool (Administration > Invoice > Purchase Order Configuration)' - valuable because the settings topic configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md returns grep -c 'Purchase Order Configuration' = 0. Corroborated cross-directory by manage-images-03021850.md: 'The PO configuration associated with a Group may also include supporting documents.' and 'These documents apply to all PO transmissions performed by the PO Processor for that Group and are included alongside any documents added by the user.'
orphanCandidates.whatWouldFixIt: A field named 'Include in PO Transmission' on whichever page owns the purchase request / PO processing forms - not yet built. Three of the four entries would then be dependencies on that field rather than values here.

orphanCandidates.enumerates: Email Message Replacement Tokens - the 4-row Variable | Label Name | Description table. LISTED HERE AS A REJECTED NEAR-MISS, not as a candidate for wiring.
orphanCandidates.whyNoOwner: DELIBERATELY REJECTED. Purchase Order Configuration's default_email_subject_when_transmitting_purchase_orders field is documented as offering tokens - 'When the admin clicks the Default Email Subject When Transmitting Purchase Orders field, they will see a tool tip with information (tokens) about how to enter text in the field.' - but that tooltip's token list is NEVER published anywhere in the corpus. This table is a DIFFERENT feature: it belongs to reminder emails on the Add Email Reminder page ('When creating an email message for a reminder, you can add dynamic text to the subject line and the email message body text.'), and its tokens are scoped to reminder-rule queries. Wiring it to a PO transmittal field would be a wrong owner of exactly the kind this build has been burned by. Recorded so a later run does not rediscover it and wire it. Label Name and Description per row, verbatim: %1% = Logon URL, 'The URL for the Concur Sign In page.'; %2% = User Name, 'The primary recipient of the email in this format: First-name Last-name. This does not pertain to any Copy To recipients, such as approvers.'; %3% = Number of Records, 'The number of applicable object records, such as number of invoices, found by the reminder rule query, which is based on the Reminder Type.'; %4% = List of Records, 'A list of the applicable object records found by the reminder rule query, based on pre-defined formats. This variable is not supported in the Email Subject field.' Constraint on all four: 'You cannot select any of these replacement token variables from the Helper pane to have them appear automatically in the Email Subject or Email Message fields. You must type the variables manually.'
orphanCandidates.whatWouldFixIt: SAP publishing the PO transmittal tooltip's own token roster, or an Email Reminders page node that owns this table properly. Until one exists, default_email_subject_when_transmitting_purchase_orders stays unenumerated and that is the correct answer.
